summary: A 1976 list of assigned network numbers for the ARPANET and connected networks. It is a registry-style document and is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 717 records network numbers assigned for internetwork experiments and shows how those numbers fit into an internetwork header. The RFC is Historic.

questions: which network numbers did rfc 717 assign
what fields are in the internetwork header
what did the format field select
subtitle: An assigned-number list and header description for early internetwork experiments.

tldr.problem: Inter-network protocol experiments needed network numbers to identify participating networks.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists four assigned network numbers and reproduces an internetwork header with destination and source network and host fields.
tldr.outcome: RFC 717 records the assignments and header formats used for the experiments. Its status is Historic.

today: RFC 717 is Historic. It records network assignments and header formats for the inter-network protocol experiments described in the memo.

sections.title: Assigned Network Numbers
sections.content:
The note lists four assignments: BBNRCCnet has decimal number 3, SanFranPRnet 7, ARPANET 10, and BostonPRnet 11. It says additional numbers are assigned by Jon Postel.

These numbers identify networks for use in the inter-network protocol experiments described by the memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo lists four networks and the numbers assigned to them for experiments. It also names the person to contact about additional assignments.

sections.title: Internetwork Header Fields
sections.content:
The reproduced protocol-independent header uses 8 bits for the destination network and 24 bits for the destination host, followed by equivalent source fields. It also carries data length, header length, and a four-bit Format field.

The Format value selects gateway processing and the destination protocol module. The memo lists values for Escape, TCP, Secure TCP, and Cross Internet Debugging.
sections.plainLanguage: The header identifies the source and destination network and host. A format value tells the gateway which protocol processing to use.

sections.title: TCP-Specific Header Information
sections.content:
The memo also reproduces a TCP-specific header containing a protocol version, sequence number, window, control field, ports, acknowledgement number, and checksum. A separate short TCP-specific layout is included.

These layouts are presented as the current headers for the inter-network protocol experiments.
sections.plainLanguage: The TCP-specific portion carries connection and data-transfer information, including sequence and acknowledgement numbers and port values.
